title: Sell Mineral Rights in Kaycee, WY
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Kaycee, WY | Johnson County
metaDescription: Kaycee, WY mineral owner near Hole-in-the-Wall and the Barnum field? Get a fair cash offer for your Johnson County mineral or royalty interest.
heroLead: Kaycee sits at the southern edge of the Powder River Basin, cattle country made famous by Hole-in-the-Wall, and legacy oil fields like Barnum that have quietly produced for decades.
intro: The town's outlaw history gets more attention than its oil history, but both run through the same ranching families who've held this ground since the early 1900s. If you're holding minerals here, they likely came down through a homestead patent or an old ranch transaction, same as most of the county.

sections.heading: Barnum field and the basin's southern edge
paragraphs: Barnum and similar legacy structures near Kaycee have produced steadily since discovery, mostly stripper-level output at this point, operated by independents who've held the leases through several ownership changes. Newer horizontal targets in the Niobrara and Turner have reached into parts of the area as well, layering fresh activity onto old production.

sections.heading: Split estate is common on Kaycee ranches
paragraphs: A lot of ranch land around Kaycee carries federally reserved minerals under privately owned surface, a legacy of Stock-Raising Homestead Act patents from a century ago. Confirming whether you own the minerals under your own ranch, or just the surface, is the first real step before any sale conversation.

sections.heading: What to bring to the table
paragraphs: Your deed, legal description, and any production history you have. If your interest is producing, recent check stubs speed things up considerably. If it's undeveloped, expect a conservative offer reflecting speculative rather than proven value.

sections.heading: Outlaw history and oil history running side by side
paragraphs: The same rugged terrain that made Hole-in-the-Wall a hideout for outlaws in the 1890s also kept early oil surveyors from fully mapping this corner of Johnson County until later than surrounding areas. That later start means some Kaycee-area mineral histories are shorter and cleaner than the century-plus chains found closer to Casper or Douglas.

faqs.question: Does my Kaycee ranch include the mineral rights?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Check whether your patent reserved minerals to the federal government under the Stock-Raising Homestead Act, which was common in this area.

faqs.question: Is Barnum field still producing?
faqs.answer: Yes, mostly stripper-level production from a legacy field, with some newer horizontal activity nearby. Confirm your specific tract through Johnson County Clerk records in Buffalo.

faqs.question: Can I sell minerals my family has held for generations?
faqs.answer: Yes, long-held interests sell the same as recently acquired ones. What matters is confirming your current ownership percentage and production status.

faqs.question: Does a shorter mineral history make selling easier?
faqs.answer: Often, yes. Fewer generations of transfers generally means a cleaner, faster title review, though production status and acreage still drive the actual offer.
